Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

neither … nor conjunction

also not … or, nor … nor

classical

Sen. Ep. 27.8: bona mēns nec commodātur nec emitur
Liv. praef. 6: ea nec adfirmāre nec refellere in animō est

neque … neque (nec … nec)

conjunctions, before each member

In commands and purpose clauses, nēve … nēve (neu … neu).

Other words

  • nēve … nēve (neu … neu) — neither … nor (in commands and purpose)

    conjunctions, with the subjunctive or imperative · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 37: neu caedās, neu tangās (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • bona mēns nec commodātur nec emitur

    good sense can be neither borrowed nor boughtSen. Ep. 27.8

  • ea nec adfirmāre nec refellere in animō est

    I mean neither to vouch for these things nor to refute themLiv. praef. 6

  • nam nec ipse meōrum lūsibus nec illī studiīs meīs obstrepunt

    for neither do I disturb my household’s games, nor they my workPlin. Ep. 2.17.24

  • quae nec pernumerāre cūriōsī possint

    which the curious could not countCatull. 7.11–12

See also and not, either … or, not.

SourcesLewis & Short: neque · Lewis & Short: neve

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
